```{r load library, include=FALSE}
library(psych)
library(car)
library(knitr)
library(broom)

# needed libraries
library(pairwiseComparisons) #https://indrajeetpatil.github.io/pairwiseComparisons/
library(ggsignif)
library(kableExtra)

library(scales)

library(reshape2)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r load data, include=FALSE}

load("~/Dropbox/Medaglia_RiskBenefit_Neuroethics/Pilot_Data/Study1_Project/RiskBenefit_Neuroethics/data/Cleaned_Pilot/clean.data.2020.09.27.RData")
# Disable scientific notation
options(scipen=999)


Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
   dplyr::select("user_id", "condition", "Risk_Beta", "Gain_Beta", "Interaction", 
"Risk_sig", "Gain_sig", "Interaction_sig", "vif.risk", "vif.gain", 
"vif.interaction", "marginal.effect.risk", "marginal.effect.gain", 
"marginal.effect.interaction", "No", "Yes", 
"Extraversion", "Agreeableness", "Conscientiousness", "Neuroticism", 
"Openness", "Harm", "Fairness", "Loyalty", "Athority", "Sancticy", 
"PerspectiveTaking", "Fantasy", "EmpathicConcern", "PersonalDistress", 
"POWER", "SELF.DIRECTION", "ACHIEVEMENT", "HEDONISM", "STIMULATION", 
"UNIVERSALISM", "BENEVOLENCE", "TRADITION", "CONFORMITY", "SECURITY", 
"Lying", "Assasination", "Torture", "Murder", "Stealing", "ForcedSterilization", 
"consequentialism.score", "moral.commitment", "SNS.total", "SNS.ability", 
"SNS.preference", "Berlin1", "Berlin2", "Berlin3", "Berlin4", 
"BerlinScore", "GRiPs_Score", "republican", "democrat", "independent", 
"conservative", "liberal", "conservatismFactor", "sex", "age", 
"race_ethnicity", "education", "ReligionRaised", "ReligionNow", 
"Religiosity", "Spirituality", "AttendChurch", "ReligiousActivity", 
"meditation", "RelationshipStatus", "Income", "YearOfEducation", "Political_Party", "Optimize"
) %>% 
   mutate(lambda = -Risk_Beta/Gain_Beta) %>%
   mutate(Risk_odds = exp(Risk_Beta)) %>%
   mutate(Gain_odds = exp(Gain_Beta)) %>%
   mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.80 | No >= 75 *.80, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
   mutate(loss_aversion = as.factor(ifelse(lambda > 1, "loss_aversion", "Not_loss_aversion"))) %>% 
   mutate(risk_aversion = as.factor(ifelse(Risk_odds > 1, "risk_seeking", "risk_aversion"))) %>% 
   distinct() -> data.h
```


```{r values, echo=FALSE}
data.h %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, condition, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, "POWER", "SELF.DIRECTION", 
"ACHIEVEMENT", "HEDONISM", "STIMULATION", "UNIVERSALISM", "BENEVOLENCE", 
"TRADITION", "CONFORMITY", "SECURITY", Yes, No) -> data.values
data.values$condition <- relevel(data.values$condition, "Mood")

#note you need to run the controls for Yes's still

#risk 
lm.power.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~POWER, data.values)
lm.self.direction.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~SELF.DIRECTION, data.values)
lm.achievement.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~ACHIEVEMENT, data.values)
lm.hedonism.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~HEDONISM, data.values)
lm.stimulation.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~STIMULATION, data.values)
lm.universalism.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~UNIVERSALISM, data.values)
lm.benevolence.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~BENEVOLENCE, data.values)
lm.tradition.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~TRADITION, data.values)
lm.conformity.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~CONFORMITY, data.values)
lm.security.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~SECURITY, data.values)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.power.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Risk given Continuous POWER")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

data.values %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, POWER, SELF.DIRECTION, ACHIEVEMENT, HEDONISM, STIMULATION, UNIVERSALISM, BENEVOLENCE, TRADITION, CONFORMITY, SECURITY) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = "user_id" , variable.name = "value", value.name = "likert") -> plotdata

plotdata <- merge(data.values[,c("user_id", "marginal.effect.risk")], plotdata, "user_id")

values <- plotdata %>%
  group_by(value, likert) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(marginal.effect.risk),
         sd = sd(marginal.effect.risk),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n)) %>% na.omit()

knitr::kable(values, caption = "Descriptives for risk by value")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
pd <- position_dodge(0.2)
ggplot(values, 
       aes(x = likert,
           y = mean, 
           group=value, 
           color=value)) +
   geom_point(position=pd, 
             size = 3) +
  geom_line(position = pd, 
            size = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1, 
                position = pd, 
                size = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Mean risk AME by value",
       subtitle = "(mean +/- standard error)",
       x = "", 
       y = "",
       color = "Attribute")+
  facet_wrap(~ value)+
  theme(legend.position="none")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype="dashed", size=.5)
```

**risk can be predicted by self direction, tradition, conformity, security**

**gain can be predicted by henonism**


```{r lombrozo, echo=FALSE}
data.h %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, "Lying", "Assasination", 
"Torture", "Murder", "Stealing", "ForcedSterilization", "consequentialism.score", 
"moral.commitment", Yes, No) -> data.commitment

data.commitment$moral.commitment <- relevel(data.commitment$moral.commitment, "Deontological")

#risk 
lm.commitment.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~consequentialism.score, data.commitment)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.commitment.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Risk given Continuous consequentialism")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

lm.commitment.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~moral.commitment, data.commitment)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.commitment.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Risk given Categorical moral commitment")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

ggplot(data.commitment, aes(x=consequentialism.score, y=marginal.effect.risk)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +
    geom_point() + 
    labs(x = "consequentialism.score", 
       y = "Risk", 
       title  = "Risk by consequentialism.score")

moral <- data.commitment %>%
  group_by(moral.commitment) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(marginal.effect.risk),
         sd = sd(marginal.effect.risk),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n)) %>% na.omit()
knitr::kable(moral, caption = "Descriptives for risk by moral commitment")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
ggplot(moral, 
       aes(x = moral.commitment, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1) +
   labs(x = "moral.commitment", 
       y = "Mean", 
       title  = "Risk by moral commitment")

# creating a basic plot
p <- ggplot(data.commitment, aes(moral.commitment, marginal.effect.risk, fill = moral.commitment)) +
  geom_boxplot()

# using `pairwiseComparisons` package to create a dataframe with results
df <-
  pairwise_comparisons(data.commitment, moral.commitment, marginal.effect.risk, messages = FALSE, p.adjust.method = "none", var.equal = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.data = ., groups = purrr::pmap(.l = list(group1, group2), .f = c)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data = ., group1)
knitr::kable(df[c("group1", "group2", "p.value", "significance", "test.details")], caption = "Pairwise comparisons for risk by moral.commitment")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

p +
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
    comparisons = df$groups,
    map_signif_level = TRUE,
    tip_length = 0.01,
    y_position = c(-0.01, .02, .001),
    annotations = df$label,
    test = NULL,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    parse = TRUE
  )

knitr::kable(moral, caption = "Descriptives for gain by moral commitment")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
ggplot(moral, 
       aes(x = moral.commitment, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1) +
   labs(x = "moral.commitment", 
       y = "Mean", 
       title  = "gain by moral commitment")

# creating a basic plot
p <- ggplot(data.commitment, aes(moral.commitment, marginal.effect.gain, fill = moral.commitment)) +
  geom_boxplot()

# using `pairwiseComparisons` package to create a dataframe with results
df <-
  pairwise_comparisons(data.commitment, moral.commitment, marginal.effect.gain, messages = FALSE, p.adjust.method = "none", var.equal = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.data = ., groups = purrr::pmap(.l = list(group1, group2), .f = c)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data = ., group1)
knitr::kable(df[c("group1", "group2", "p.value", "significance", "test.details")], caption = "Pairwise comparisons for gain by moral.commitment")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

p +
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
    comparisons = df$groups,
    map_signif_level = TRUE,
    tip_length = 0.01,
    y_position = c(-0.01, .02, .001),
    annotations = df$label,
    test = NULL,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    parse = TRUE
  )


###both in one graph
data.commitment %>% 
  dplyr::select(moral.commitment, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain) %>% 
  mutate(marginal.effect.risk = -marginal.effect.risk) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = "moral.commitment" , variable.name = "type", value.name = "beta") -> plotdata

political <- plotdata %>%
  group_by(moral.commitment, type) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean = mean(beta),
            sd = sd(beta),
            se = sd/sqrt(n))

pd <- position_dodge(0.2)
ggplot(political, 
       aes(x = factor(moral.commitment, 
                      labels = c("Deontological",
                                 "Consequentialist")), 
           y = mean, 
           group=type, 
           color=type)) +
  geom_point(position=pd, 
             size = 3) +
  geom_line(position = pd, 
            size = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1, 
                position = pd, 
                size = 1) +
  #scale_y_continuous(label = scales::dollar) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette="Set1") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Mean AME by type and moral commitment",
       subtitle = "(mean +/- standard error)",
       x = "", 
       y = "",
       color = "Attribute")

#testing the interaction between r/b and moral commitment contoling for the effect of dom responses
data.commitment %>% 
  dplyr::select(moral.commitment, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, Yes, No) %>% 
  mutate(marginal.effect.risk = -marginal.effect.risk) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = c("moral.commitment", "Yes", "No") , variable.name = "type", value.name = "beta") -> test

lm.commitment <- lm(beta~ type*moral.commitment, test)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.commitment), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting AME gien R/B and moral commitment")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
```

the subjective numeracy score has subscales, so I tested those too. 

Here we see both numeracy measures can predict risk. Looking even closer, the subjective numeracy scale seems to do a better job

**Adjusted R-squared for predicting risk with objective:  0.04239**

**Adjusted R-squared for predicting risk with subjective subscale:  0.05298**

However, the subjective measure seems to be leveraged by a few points

**If you look at both in a model controling for yes, they each contribute to predicting risk**
see the table with both measures
